page_title: Spool — the Mac email client that doesn't get slower

sources.entry: Spool - Keyboard-driven email client written in Rust on gpui, the framework Zed is built with. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/wes/spool) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Spool
summary.one_liner: Spool is a free, open-source, keyboard-driven Mac email client written in Rust on the gpui GPU-accelerated UI framework (the one Zed uses), with no web view around the app.
use_cases: Reading and triaging a large mailbox quickly from the keyboard
Connecting a Gmail or other IMAP account on a Mac
Full-text searching years of archived mail
Composing and replying to mail in separate windows
Benchmarking email client performance on large mailboxes
Reading newsletters and receipts with remote images blocked
summary.what_it_does: Spool is a macOS email client with an IMAP client, SQLite storage with an FTS5 full-text index, and threaded conversations. It connects to Gmail via OAuth (PKCE, loopback redirect) or to any IMAP server with a password, stores secrets in the keychain, and syncs locally with IDLE for new mail. The list is virtualized and drawn on the GPU, and the page reports microsecond frame-build times and sub-120 ms opens at 250,000 messages on an M-series MacBook. Mail is read in a WKWebView with scripts removed, navigation blocked, and remote images blocked by default; plain-text rendering is available. Search supports operators such as from:, to:, subject:, is:unread, has:attachment, and date filters, and archive, move, and flag actions are queued to the server.
notable: Rust app on gpui (the framework Zed uses), GPU-drawn with no Electron or browser shell
Published benchmarks against Apple Mail, MailMate, Thunderbird, Canary and Mailflare, with a spool --bench command to reproduce them
Blocks remote images and scripts in HTML mail, with per-message consent for images
Open source under MIT; signed and notarized macOS app
caveats: Free during the beta only; the version number signals it has not been tested broadly with other people's mail
Only the macOS reader uses a web view; other platforms fall back to the plain block renderer, and the app is Mac-only in practice
Archive, move and flag changes made on other devices do not sync back; drafts list and IMAP Drafts sync are not yet built
